title: Activation mode selects fluoride loss versus fluorine-retentive P(O)H addition
relation: For a compatible gem-difluoroalkene and P(O)H partner, polar addition under basic conditions can form a carbanion that loses fluoride; peroxide-initiated radical addition followed by H-atom transfer instead can furnish a saturated CF2-containing product.

preconditions.radical_regime: peroxide-initiated hydrophosphinylation with compatible P(O)H donor

directional_predictions.when: p-methoxy gem-difluorostyrene + Ph2P(O)H under Intelli peroxide conditions
directional_predictions.then: CF2-retaining saturated adduct supported, an alternative endpoint to monofluoroalkene

directional_predictions.when: nitro-substituted alkene or diethyl phosphite in peroxide conditions
directional_predictions.then: do not apply the default CF2-retention/productive-addition prediction

project_transfer: Carbonyl-bearing CF3 starting materials require additional activation steps; do not infer success or failure from this local alkene rule.
prediction_uncertainty: Not a calibrated probability; unknown outside specified scope

title: Donor-dependent acid response determines whether a fluorovinyl product undergoes HF addition
relation: A fluorovinyl ether that has already formed can be consumed by hydrofluorination when the HF/coacid combination enables productive protonation and fluoride capture. The required regime depends on the attached heteroatom substituent; successful monofluoro formation and successful HF addition are separate outcomes.

preconditions.formed_product: source-characterized fluorovinyl ether, thioether, enamine or phosphine

directional_predictions.when: model alkoxy fluorovinyl ether 3 + NEt3·3HF, then add TFA in PhMe
directional_predictions.then: productive conversion toward CF2 ether increases; reported99% endpoint

directional_predictions.when: change alkoxy to aryloxy or thioether product
directional_predictions.then: do not transfer model TFA recipe without adjustment; stronger/different acid systems used

directional_predictions.when: Ph2PH or N-methylaniline gives monofluorovinyl intermediate but subsequent HF addition fails
directional_predictions.then: label monoF formation positive and subsequent CF2 formation negative separately

project_transfer: Use stage-resolved endpoint bookkeeping for this project; acid response of its conjugated carbonyl monofluoro products is unknown.
prediction_uncertainty: No continuous kinetics or universal acid-strength ordering established

title: NiH selenium transfer requires a compatible donor and interception of nucleophilic selenium
relation: In the documented amide-directed NiH hydroselenylation, the diselenide donor is compatible with reductive selenium transfer, whereas phenylselenol is unproductive; interception of nucleophilic selenium by BnBr supports catalyst turnover.

preconditions.substrate: N-phenylbut-3-enamide or independently verified source scope

directional_predictions.when: replace PhSeH by PhSeSePh at matched Table1 conditions
directional_predictions.then: desired beta-selenide becomes productive (dash versus91% NMR)

directional_predictions.when: omit BnBr from matched PhSeSePh system

project_transfer: Ordinary nonfluorinated alkene chemistry. No positive or negative ground-truth label follows for PhSeH + project CF3 carbonyl.
prediction_uncertainty: Unknown outside the explicit NiH regime
